answer: Correlation pairs (identity attribute <-> account attribute, operation Equals/`EQ` only) are evaluated one at a time, in the configured order, and the first pair that matches correlates the account; it is an OR, not an AND of all pairs. Matching is case-insensitive by default (per-assignment `ignoreCase` via the API). Put the most reliable, unique identifier (employee number, immutable ID) first and names last or never. Only searchable identity attributes can be used (identities must be processed first) and account values over 128 characters are not supported. If no configured pair matches, ISC falls back to default correlation: account name compared with the identity `name` (case-insensitive, not configurable). If that also fails the account stays uncorrelated (no access, not governed) until you fix data/config, use a Correlation rule (`accountCorrelationRule`), or correlate manually with the correlation file. Config API: `GET/PUT /sources/v1/{id}/correlation-config` (`attributeAssignments` with `property`, `value`, `operation: EQ`, `ignoreCase`, `matchMode`).

UI-started aggregations are always optimized: accounts whose data did not change since the last aggregation are skipped, and correlation (and manager correlation) is not re-evaluated for them, so old uncorrelated accounts stay uncorrelated. Fix: run one unoptimized aggregation via the API, `POST /sources/v1/{id}/load-accounts` as `multipart/form-data` with field `disableOptimization=true` (applies to that run only); track it with `GET /account-aggregations/v1/{taskId}/status`. If accounts still do not correlate, check that the identity attribute is searchable and populated after identity processing, value formats match (leading zeros, domain prefixes, case), values are unique, and the account attribute is in the account schema. Manually correlated accounts (`manuallyCorrelated=true`) are not changed by unoptimized aggregation. Remaining ones can be correlated with the correlation file (`POST /sources/v1/{id}/load-uncorrelated-accounts`).

Accounts missing from the source are removed from ISC only if Enable Account Deletion is on, and only by full account aggregations (schedule, Start Aggregation, `POST /sources/v1/{id}/load-accounts`); delta aggregations and single-account reloads (`POST /accounts/v1/{id}/reload`) never delete. The delete threshold (source field `deleteThreshold`, 0-100) is a percentage of the source's accounts: if an aggregation would delete more than that, the delete phase is skipped and a warning is raised (account deletion skipped, threshold exceeded), and the accounts stay until you fix the source or raise the threshold for one run. On small sources the percentage is rounded to whole accounts; if it rounds below one account only a 100% deletion is blocked. Typical value is low (about 10%) so an empty/truncated read (VA problem, wrong base DN, empty file) cannot wipe access. Enable deletion and set the threshold only after the first clean aggregations.

Create profile fields are computed top to bottom, so a Static (Velocity) value can only reference fields defined earlier. Because `uid` (generator `Create Unique Account ID`, i.e. transform `{"type":"rule","attributes":{"name":"Create Unique Account ID"}}`) is below `mail`, `$uid` is not yet computed when `mail` is evaluated, so mail comes out empty/literal or wrong. Fix: move the `uid` field above `mail` in the policy's `fields` array, keep `mail` as `{"type":"static","attributes":{"value":"$uid@corp.com"}}`. Static values cannot read identity attributes directly (map them to an earlier field first), and generator templates cannot read other create-profile fields at all. If mail itself must be unique, use the `Create Unique LDAP Attribute` generator instead. Apply via `GET /sources/v1/{sourceId}/provisioning-policies/CREATE`, reorder, validate with `scripts/check_source_config.py` (it flags static values that reference later fields), then `PUT` back.

Attribute sync only updates existing, correlated accounts: it never creates accounts and ignores uncorrelated ones. An attribute can be synced only if it is in Create Account and mapped directly from an identity attribute (not via a transform/generator); the built-in Manager attribute cannot be synced. Comparison is case-sensitive, nulls are propagated, and multi-valued attributes need custom rules. Bulk Sync per source is limited to at most 3 full syncs per 24 hours and only when the source is healthy; failed syncs are retried up to 10 times. It may overwrite native changes on synced attributes, and attributes also changed by rules or aggregation never converge and keep retrying. Config API is experimental: `GET/PUT /sources/v1/{id}/attribute-sync-config`, `POST /sources/v1/{id}/synchronize-attributes` (header `X-SailPoint-Experimental: true`).

Use `POST /sources/v1/{sourceId}/schedules` (scope `idn:sources:manage`, ORG_ADMIN/SOURCE_ADMIN/SOURCE_SUBADMIN) with body `{"type": "ACCOUNT_AGGREGATION", "cronExpression": "0 0 5,13,21 * * ?"}`, and a second call with `"type": "GROUP_AGGREGATION"` for entitlements. `cronExpression` is a Quartz cron (seconds first, `?` in day-of-month or day-of-week, days of week 1-7 = Sunday-Saturday). One schedule per type: read with `GET /sources/v1/{sourceId}/schedules[/{scheduleType}]`, change with `PATCH /sources/v1/{sourceId}/schedules/{scheduleType}` (JSON Patch, `type` immutable), remove with `DELETE .../schedules/{scheduleType}`. Times run in the VA cluster's time zone and do not follow DST. Quick Compliance sources allow at most 3 runs a day, 8 hours apart (not for Org Admins). For one-off runs use `POST /sources/v1/{id}/load-accounts` and `POST /sources/v1/{sourceId}/load-entitlements`.

NCD only finds changes when an account aggregation runs, by comparing what it reads with what ISC stored, so check that aggregations are actually running (scheduled/full). In the config (`GET/PUT /sources/v1/{sourceId}/native-change-detection-config`) `enabled` must be true, at least one operation (`ACCOUNT_CREATED`, `ACCOUNT_UPDATED`, `ACCOUNT_DELETED`) must be selected, and at least one attribute (`allEntitlements`, `allNonEntitlementAttributes`, `selectedEntitlements`, `selectedNonEntitlementAttributes`); for Updated, the changed attribute must be a monitored one. Check the trigger subscription exists and is enabled for Native Change Account Created/Updated/Deleted, and that any JSONPath filter does not drop the events. Look for audit events Create/Update/Delete Native Change Detected to see whether detection happened. NCD is not available for Non-Employee sources, and SAML Just-in-Time sources must be configured through the API. Also, an optimized aggregation of unchanged data yields nothing to detect, and attribute sync may revert native changes.

The Create Account profile is the provisioning policy with `usageType: CREATE`: read it with `GET /sources/v1/{sourceId}/provisioning-policies/CREATE`, edit, and `PUT` the whole object back to the same path (or `PATCH` with JSON Patch); create one with `POST /sources/v1/{sourceId}/provisioning-policies`, several at once with `POST .../provisioning-policies/bulk-update`. Body: `name`, `description`, `usageType`, `fields[]` (each with `name` case-sensitive account attribute, `type` string/int/long/date/boolean/secret, `isRequired`, `isMultiValued`, `transform`, `attributes`); field order matters. In v1 there is one policy per usage type, so a source cannot have several CREATE policies. Several policies per usage type exist only through the experimental v2 API by id, `/sources/v2/{sourceId}/provisioning-policies[/{id}]` (header `X-SailPoint-Experimental: true`), used for source subtypes / machine accounts (`subtypeId`, `CREATE_MACHINE_ACCOUNT`). Validate first with `scripts/check_source_config.py`.

List them with `GET /accounts/v1?filters=sourceId eq "<sourceId>" and uncorrelated eq true` (page with `limit`/`offset`); identity search does not see uncorrelated accounts. In the UI there is also Account Management > Uncorrelated Accounts and the Uncorrelated Accounts report (Admin > Global > Reports). To correlate in bulk, download the correlation file (Uncorrelated Accounts > Download Correlation File), fill the target identity's account ID in `userName`, and upload it with `POST /sources/v1/{id}/load-uncorrelated-accounts` (`multipart/form-data`, field `file`, scope `idn:sources:manage`, ORG_ADMIN; returns 202 with a task). Those links are stored as `manuallyCorrelated=true` and are not undone by unoptimized aggregation; up to 100 accounts per identity. If the cause is a correlation config problem, fix the config and run `load-accounts` with `disableOptimization=true` instead.

No. The `features` array describes what the connector implements (`PROVISIONING` means the connector can read and write accounts and implements provision()); the API spec warns that modifying it may cause unsupportable source configuration errors and recommends not modifying it for SailPoint-supported connectors. Adding the flag does not add write capability; it can break the source. Enable provisioning through the supported connector configuration instead (for JDBC, the connector's provisioning settings/scripts or JDBC provisioning connector rules, see isc-rules), plus a Create Account profile (`provisioning-policies/CREATE`). The skill's checker flags unknown features but the rule is: do not touch `features` on SailPoint-supported connectors.
